title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (Longue Marche, section on sections of the fundamental group of a relative curve, local behaviour at a cusp). The setting is as follows.
- S = Spec V is a trait (henselian, presumably strictly henselian), with generic point η and closed point s.
- X/S is a smooth relative curve (the margin says the dimension should not matter). T ⊂ X is a finite étale divisor, a union of sections g_i (i ∈ I, ν = card I), and U = X \ T.
- f: S → X is a section with f(η) ∈ U, but f(s) = g_{i0}(s) = x. So the S-point of U 'tends to the cusp i0'.
- f|η gives a homomorphism π_1(η) → π_1(U). Restricted to the (prime-to-p, tame) inertia T = Ẑ'(1), one wants to compute it.

The previous page explains why. A homological criterion looks at the induced map (11) T_ℓ → T_ℓ^I/T_ℓ. This is the toric part G_m^I/G_m of the generalized Jacobian of U, i.e. the cusp loops modulo the global relation. One needs this map to be nonzero to conclude.

This page states the guess.
- Let A = O_{X,x}, a 2-dimensional regular local ring.
- Let J_{g_{i0}} and J_f be the kernels of g_{i0}^*, f^*: A → V. They are invertible ideals, since sections of a smooth morphism are regular immersions of codimension 1.
- Define μ = length V/g_{i0}^*(J_f). This is finite and nonzero because f ≠ g_{i0}.
- μ is symmetric in f and g_{i0}, because V/g^*(J_f) ≅ A/(J_g + J_f). That is the length of the local artinian scheme f(S) ∩ g_{i0}(S), i.e. the intersection multiplicity of the two section curves at x.

Conjecture: the map T_ℓ → T_ℓ^I/T_ℓ is μ times the canonical map T_ℓ → T_ℓ^I given by the i0-th coordinate. ("Il faudrait que je demande à Carlos de me le confirmer".)

For ν = 1 the target T_ℓ^I/T_ℓ is 0, so the homological criterion is useless. The case needs separate treatment, and he reformulates at the level of prime-to-p fundamental groups: π_1(η) → π_1(U) ≅ π_1(U_s) restricted to inertia should equal k_{i0} ∘ (μ·id_T). Here k_{i0}: T → π_1(U_s) is the local homomorphism, the inertia/meridian at the cusp i0 (next page, (12)), and he 'admits' it.

The margin notes this should be independent of dim X. In other words: for a smooth divisor T in any smooth X, a trait meeting T with multiplicity μ sends the inertia generator to the μ-th power of the meridian.

The justification is Kummer/Abhyankar. Locally U ⊃ Spec A[1/t], with t a generator of J_{g_{i0}}. Then f^*(t) = (unit)·π^μ. Tame covers are obtained by extracting n-th roots of t (and units), so the inertia generator maps to the μ-th power of the meridian.
errors: No real error. The conjectured formula is correct and is essentially the standard Kummer-theoretic computation: valuation of f^*(local equation of the cusp) = μ.

π_1(U) ≅ π_1(U_s) only holds as stated for prime-to-p (or tame) quotients over a strictly henselian base, with the geometric fundamental group. He does add the 'premiers à p' qualifier, but the identification is used loosely.

The homological statement determines only the image in T_ℓ^I/T_ℓ. Grothendieck's guess 'μ times the i0-th canonical map' is consistent with the π_1 statement, but the latter is stronger. That is why ν = 1 needs the π_1 version.

ideas.what: Symmetric intersection-multiplicity invariant μ = length V/g^*(J_f) = length A/(J_g+J_f) of two sections of a relative curve meeting on the special fibre
ideas.modern_name: local intersection multiplicity of two sections (arithmetic intersection number at a point)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Serre's intersection multiplicity / arithmetic surfaces, Arakelov theory)

ideas.what: Inertia of an S-point of U specializing to a cusp maps to the μ-th power of the cusp inertia generator (k_{i0} ∘ μ)
ideas.modern_name: image of inertia under sections/points reducing to a cusp; cuspidal (packet) sections; tame Kummer computation
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore. Appears in the section-conjecture literature (Nakamura on tangential base points and cuspidal packets; Stix's book, discussion of points reducing to cusps / cuspidal sections)

ideas.what: Using the toric part G_m^I/G_m of the generalized Jacobian (H_1 of U with ℓ-adic coefficients) as a homological criterion to detect the cusp that a point specializes to
ideas.modern_name: abelianized / homological section obstruction via generalized Jacobian (cuspidal sections detected in H_1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: later section-conjecture literature (e.g. Stix, Saïdi, Hoshi on cuspidal sections)

missed.claim: Historical detail: Grothendieck intended to have the generalized-Jacobian/inertia computation confirmed by 'Carlos', almost certainly Carlos Contou-Carrère, his Montpellier student who worked on generalized and local Jacobians. This documents a small collaboration on the Longue Marche material (c. 1981) that is not in the record.
missed.quote: Il faudrait que je demande à Carlos de me le confirmer.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is relevant to the history of the Longue Marche and of Contou-Carrère's work (the Contou-Carrère symbol, local Jacobians), and of how cuspidal behaviour of sections was approached.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but standard local computation: inertia maps to the μ-th power of the cusp meridian, with μ the intersection multiplicity. It anticipates later work on cuspidal sections, but a specialist would find it routine. The only mildly notable point is the reference to 'Carlos' (Contou-Carrère).
transcription_corrections: Line 3 should read V/g_{i_0}^*(J_f) ≃ A/(J_{g_{i_0}} + J_f) (pullback star on g_{i_0}).
The interlinear insertion above 'intersection des' reads '$x_s$-schémas' (or similar); the phrase is 'intersection des [x_s-schémas] f(S) et g_{i_0}(S) de X'.
'le produit par μ des homomorphismes canoniques' — the [?] can be dropped.
Left margin: 'Ceci doit être indépendant de la dimension de X !' appears plausible.
'que que l'homom. ext.' is a dittography; read 'que l'homom. ext. π_1(η) → π_1(U) ≃ π_1(U_s)'.
